original_question: What is the computational complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?
target_in_paper: Section 11, “Open Problems,” under “Complexity Analysis and Security,” item 1: “What is the complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups?” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s official open problem almost verbatim, keeps the scope exactly on polycyclic groups, and asks about the search conjugacy problem rather than a neighboring problem such as the decision conjugacy problem, twisted search conjugacy problem, generic-case complexity, or quantum variants. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
missing_details: A stand-alone version should specify the input model: the paper’s surrounding context treats polycyclic groups via finite, and in practice consistent, polycyclic presentations with unique normal forms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

It should define the search conjugacy problem explicitly: given conjugate elements u,v in a polycyclic group G, compute a conjugator x that sends u to v by conjugation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

It should say that the complexity sought is worst-case time complexity; the paper separately lists the generic-case complexity of the same problem as a different open problem, so the two should not be merged. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
It should quantify over arbitrary polycyclic groups G, not only a fixed example or a special subclass. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

For full faithfulness to the paper’s context, it helps to note that solvability is already known for polycyclic groups because they embed in GL(n,Z); the open point is the complexity, not existence of an algorithm. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
refined_question: For an arbitrary polycyclic group G, given by a consistent polycyclic presentation so that elements are represented in normal form, what is the worst-case time complexity of the search conjugacy problem: on input two conjugate elements u,v∈G, compute a conjugator x∈G such that x^{-1}ux=v? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
justification: This refinement is the closest stand-alone version of the paper’s actual target because Section 11 states the open problem in exactly this scope, with no extra hypotheses beyond “polycyclic groups.” Section 8 supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make the question self-contained: polycyclic groups are discussed via consistent polycyclic presentations with unique normal forms; the search conjugacy problem is already known to be solvable in polycyclic groups via their embedding in GL(n,Z); and the authors explicitly say that the complexity is unknown, though widely conjectured to be exponential. Section 11 also distinguishes this problem from the decision conjugacy problem, twisted search conjugacy problem, and generic-case complexity, so the refined question should remain narrowly about worst-case search conjugacy in polycyclic groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
